name: Joshua Rotenberg
body: I'm applying for the Product Marketing Manager role. I haven't held the title Product Marketing Manager before, my background is broader B2B marketing and content, but the actual work described in the posting, finding the human angle in what a product does and turning it into a story people care about, is what I've been doing for the last several years, just without that specific job title attached to it.

At Solenzo, I write the thought leadership content, newsletters, and messaging frameworks that turn what a client's business does into something a prospect actually connects with, and I build a new version of that positioning for every client rather than reusing the same story twice. At Level Agency, I produced campaign assets and conversion-focused copy while coordinating execution across internal departments, which is the same cross-functional muscle this role needs to keep a story consistent across product, sales, and customer success. And because I run my own practice, I talk to customers constantly and rebuild messaging based on what I actually hear, not just what I assume they want.

What draws me to Smartling specifically is the problem itself: making a brand's story land the same way across languages and cultures is a harder version of the same problem I solve for clients across different verticals and audiences. I'd welcome the chance to talk through how that instinct applies to your product launches.
